jobs.title: Security Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

About the role

We're hiring our first Security Operations Lead to build and run the SecOps function at Fireworks AI. As we scale our AI infrastructure platform globally, we're investing in a modern detection and response capability anchored on CrowdStrike (EDR and SIEM, 365-day retention), Console AI for ticketing, and Incident.io http://Incident.io for on-call and incident management. We have a Security Incident Response Plan (SIRP) in place that you'll build on, and you'll own the function end-to-end: standing up detection content, operationalizing our incident response playbooks, running threat intel into action, and building the operational muscle that keeps Fireworks resilient as we grow. This role sits within the Security team and will primarily support Corporate Security and own incident response broadly, while partnering closely with Security Engineering on infrastructure-related incidents — bridging both areas. This is an IC-to-manager role: you’ll start hands-on building and running the function, growing into a people leader as the team scales.

What you'll do

 - Lead the rollout, tuning, and ongoing operation of CrowdStrike across our endpoint and cloud environment and SIEM use cases, partnering with IT and Security Engineering on deployment and coverage

 - Define and operate our detection and response program: build detection content, establish triage and escalation workflows, and continuously measure and improve coverage against frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK

 - Own incident response end-to-end: operationalize our existing SIRP into detailed playbooks, run incidents, lead post-incident reviews, and drive lessons learned into program improvements

 - Stand up our security operations workflow, including SOAR automation with Incident.io http://Incident.io for alerting, on-call, and incident orchestration, while also defining how incidents self-submitted through our IT ticketing system are triaged and handled as one-off cases — along with the SLAs and metrics the function runs on

 - Build and operationalize a threat intelligence capability: track threats relevant to AI infrastructure and our customer base, and translate intel into detections, hardening, and tabletop scenarios

 - Partner closely with Infrastructure, Corporate Security, and other cross-functional teams across the organization, engaging as needed to support incidents and shared initiatives

How the role will grow

As the function matures, you'll have the opportunity to:

 - Hire and build the SecOps team, growing from IC to people leader

 - Expand 24x7 coverage and adjacent capabilities like cloud detection engineering, insider threat, or red team / purple team operations

 - Shape the broader security strategy as a senior leader in the function

What we're looking for

 - 7+ years in security operations, detection and response, incident response, or a closely related field

 - Hands-on experience with EDR platforms (CrowdStrike strongly preferred; SentinelOne, Defender, or similar also relevant) including detection engineering and tuning

 - Strong detection engineering background: you've written, tested, and maintained detection content at scale and understand the tradeoffs between coverage, fidelity, and analyst load

 - Demonstrated incident response leadership: you've run real incidents from triage through executive communication and post-incident review

 - Strong scripting and automation skills (Python, SOAR platforms) applied to detection, response, and reporting workflows

 - Working knowledge of cloud security operations (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and the unique telemetry, attack patterns, and response considerations of cloud-native environments

 - Experience building or significantly maturing a SecOps function, including tooling selection, process design, and metrics

 - Comfort operating in a build phase: you can write the playbook and run the playbook, and you know when to invest in process versus when to just get things done

Nice to have

 - Experience with SIEM detection engineering at scale (CrowdStrike Falcon LogScale/NG-SIEM, Splunk, Sumo Logic, Panther, or similar)

 - Experience with Incident.io http://Incident.io, PagerDuty, or comparable incident management tooling

 - Threat intelligence experience, including operationalizing intel into detection and hardening outcomes

 - Prior experience at an AI, cloud infrastructure, or high-growth SaaS company

 - Certifications such as GCIA, GCIH, GCFA, OSCP, or similar


WHY FIREWORKS?

 - Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

 - Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

 - Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

 - Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Manager, Infrastructure and R&D
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This role owns the financial analysis behind our two largest investments: GPU infrastructure and R&D. On the infrastructure side, you'll model how we contract for capacity, how efficiently we use it, and what it costs to serve inference — the drivers that determine gross margin. On the R&D side, you'll partner with Engineering, Product, Security, and IT on headcount planning, tooling and vendor spend, and the operating budget. You'll work directly with leaders across infrastructure, engineering, product, and finance. It's an early to mid-career role with real scope, built for someone with a sharp analytical foundation who wants to understand how the business actually runs and help build the function and processes that enable Fireworks to scale.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the compute model: Build and maintain the financial model for our GPU fleet — capacity commitments, utilization, cost per GPU-hour — and how all of it flows through to unit economics, gross margin, and cash.

 - Support R&D finance: Serve as a finance partner to Engineering, Product, Security, and IT. Support R&D planning end to end: headcount and hiring plans, tooling and vendor spend, and the operating budget.

 - Support capacity planning: Serve as a source of truth for what capacity we hold, what we've committed to, and what we're actually using; partner with infra on the plan of record.

 - Analyze capacity commitments: Evaluate commitment structures and contract terms with cloud and GPU providers, surface optimization opportunities, and track provider performance and credit refunds.

 - Negotiate and manage vendors: Partner on software, tooling, and infrastructure vendor negotiations and renewals, bringing the analysis that gets us better terms.

 - Get operational: Sit in infra and engineering planning, learn how utilization, scheduling, and roadmaps actually behave, and bring that reality back into the financial model.

 - Forecast and explain: Support forecasting and variance analysis for compute, cloud, and R&D spend on a monthly cadence leadership can rely on, and explain the drivers behind the numbers clearly.

 - Split research from production: Track and forecast research and experimentation compute separately from production serving, and build the framework for evaluating return on R&D investment across teams and initiatives.

 - Build the function: Establish the reporting, dashboards, and processes that make compute and R&D economics legible to leadership.

 - Support the company narrative: Contribute the compute and R&D inputs to board materials, investor updates, and fundraising processes as they come up.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4-7 years of experience beginning with investment banking, private equity, or equivalent experience — this foundation is required for the modeling and analytical rigor it builds.

 - Ideally, subsequent time in a corporate or startup finance seat (strategic finance, FP&A, or corporate development) at a technology company.

 - Expert financial modeling skills — you can build from scratch, stress-test your own assumptions, and translate outputs into clear recommendations.

 - Genuine interest in operations. You want to understand the physical and technical system underneath the numbers, not just consume its outputs.

 - Comfort with messy and imperfect data.

 - Excellent communication with technical and non-technical audiences alike — you can take a messy question from a founder or an engineer and return a clear one-page answer.

 - Comfortable being both the architect and the operator, with strong instincts for building structure where none exists and building processes to scale.

 - High ownership and a bias toward action in an environment where priorities shift and ambiguity is the default.

 - Bachelor's degree, or equivalent practical experience.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at an AI/ML, developer platform, or cloud infrastructure company, and familiarity with how companies buy and use compute.

 - Exposure to cloud, data center, or semiconductor economics — CSP contract structures, capacity commitments, accelerator utilization.

 - Experience supporting an engineering organization as a finance partner, including headcount planning and vendor costs.

 - Working knowledge of GAAP treatment for infrastructure and capitalized software development costs.

 - Experience with consumption- or usage-based revenue models and how commits and tiers are structured around them.

 - Proficiency with SQL, Python, BI tools, or an ERP such as NetSuite.

 - Enthusiasm for using AI to automate the manual parts of finance work.


WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

Engineering & Engineering Leadership, Infrastructure, Product, Security, IT, Finance & FP&A, Accounting, and Legal.


WHY FIREWORKS?

 - Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

 - Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

 - Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

 - Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance & Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.


THE ROLE

As Strategic Finance & Operations Lead, you'll sit at the intersection of revenue, go-to-market, and financial strategy — owning the financial models, pricing frameworks, and operational processes that power Fireworks' commercial engine. This is a high-visibility, high-ownership role that works directly with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Engineering leaders to drive deals forward and help the business scale intelligently.

If you love turning ambiguity into structured frameworks and enjoy being the finance partner who actually accelerates revenue (not just reports on it) — this is your role.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build dynamic financial and operating models to evaluate new sales strategies and pricing models, accelerating topline growth while balancing competitiveness with margin health

 - Work closely with sales team on customer contracts, with cross collaboration with engineering, product, and finance to operationalize and recognize new product offers

 - Identify and drive opportunities for process automation, bringing structure with a continuous lens of improvement to reduce friction and cycle time

 - Support Sales leaders with funnel analysis and pipeline visibility for sales-led accounts, turning CRM data into actionable financial insight

 - Support revenue and demand forecasting, necessary for resource allocation and planning for cross-functional stakeholders across GTM, Engineering, and Product

 - Assist with capital planning efforts, corporate finance, or investor relations, as needed


WHO YOU ARE

 - A structured thinker who moves fast. You can build a rigorous model from scratch and ship it before the week is over.

 - A cross-functional operator. You're equally comfortable in a product roadmap discussion, a sales deal review, and a finance close meeting — and you know how to earn trust across each.

 - A business partner, not a scorekeeper. You don't just report what happened; you help shape what happens next.

 - Detail-obsessed but never lost in the weeds. You hold yourself to a high standard of accuracy and can also zoom out to tell the story behind the numbers.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity. Fireworks is scaling fast. You'll build processes and frameworks where none currently exist.


QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - 4+ years of experience in strategic finance, investment banking, or management consulting

 - Demonstrated experience building financial models from scratch

 - Strong proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets; experience working with CRM data (Salesforce or equivalent)

 - Excellent communication skills — able to translate financial analysis into clear recommendations for non-finance audiences

 - Experience or strong interest in using AI agents and tooling to develop efficient workstreams that deliver high-quality results


PREFERRED

 - Experience at a high-growth SaaS or infrastructure company; prior exposure to usage-based pricing models is a strong plus

 - Familiarity with revenue recognition principles and billing systems

 - Experience designing or administering sales compensation plans

 - Comfort working with highly technical data and familiarity with SQL / BigQuery to pull and analyze data independently


WHY FIREWORKS?

 - Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

 - Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

 - Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

 - Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.
